title: IsProfiniteGroup Structure
content: Defines a profinite group as a topological group that is compact, Hausdorff, and totally disconnected. Rather than using Lean's `TopologicalGroup` class directly (which causes elaboration issues), the structure requires continuous multiplication and continuous inversion as separate fields alongside `CompactSpace`, `T2Space`, and `TotallyDisconnectedSpace`.
mathContext: A profinite group $G$ is equivalently: (1) a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, or (2) an inverse limit $\varprojlim_{i} G_i$ of finite discrete groups. The two definitions are equivalent by a theorem of Nikolov and Segal. Every open subgroup of a profinite group has finite index, and every subgroup of finite index is open (for finitely generated profinite groups).

title: IsProP: Pro-p Group Condition
content: A topological group $G$ is pro-p if every open normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ has index $[G:N] = p^k$ for some $k$. This is a typeclass, making it available for instance resolution in downstream proofs. The definition captures the property that every finite quotient of $G$ is a $p$-group, without explicitly constructing those quotients.
mathContext: A pro-$p$ group is a profinite group $G$ such that $G \cong \varprojlim G/N$ where each $G/N$ is a finite $p$-group. Equivalently, $[G:N]$ is a power of $p$ for every open normal $N$. The free pro-$p$ group on $d$ generators is the pro-$p$ completion of the free group $F_d$.

title: IsProPSubgroup: Closed Pro-p Subgroups
content: Defines a pro-p subgroup as a subgroup that is both closed (as a subset of the ambient group) and pro-p (with the subspace topology). The closedness condition is essential: in a profinite group, closed subgroups are themselves profinite, while non-closed subgroups may lack the compactness needed for the Sylow theory to work.
mathContext: In a profinite group $G$, a subgroup $H$ is closed if and only if $H = \varprojlim H/(H \cap N)$ where $N$ ranges over open normal subgroups of $G$. Closedness ensures $H$ inherits the profinite structure.

title: SylowProP: Maximal Pro-p Subgroups
content: A Sylow pro-p subgroup bundles a subgroup with proofs that it is closed, pro-p, and maximal among closed pro-p subgroups. The maximality condition states: if $H$ is closed, pro-p, and contains the Sylow subgroup, then $H$ equals the Sylow subgroup. This mirrors the classical definition where Sylow $p$-subgroups are maximal $p$-subgroups.
mathContext: A Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup $P$ of a profinite group $G$ is a maximal closed pro-$p$ subgroup. Equivalently, $P = \varprojlim P_N$ where $P_N$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of the finite quotient $G/N$. Every pro-$p$ subgroup is contained in some Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup.

title: Axiom: Pro-p Sylow Existence via Zorn's Lemma
content: The existence axiom states that every profinite group has at least one Sylow pro-p subgroup. The proof (sketched in the docstring) applies Zorn's lemma to the poset of closed pro-p subgroups ordered by inclusion. The trivial subgroup $\{e\}$ is pro-p, ensuring nonemptiness. For any chain, the closure of the union is an upper bound: it is closed by construction, and pro-p because any open normal subgroup $N$ covers the chain, and by compactness a finite subchain suffices.
mathContext: The key step: if $\{H_i\}$ is a chain of closed pro-$p$ subgroups, then $\overline{\bigcup H_i}$ is pro-$p$. For any open normal $N$, $\overline{\bigcup H_i} \cdot N / N \cong \bigcup (H_i N/N)$, and since each $H_i N/N$ is a $p$-group and the union is a directed union of $p$-groups, it is a $p$-group.

title: Axiom: Pro-p Sylow Conjugacy via Finite Approximation
content: The conjugacy axiom asserts that any two Sylow pro-p subgroups $P, Q$ are conjugate: there exists $g \in G$ with $gPg^{-1} = Q$. The proof strategy is a hallmark of profinite group theory: reduce to finite quotients, solve the finite problem, then lift back using compactness. For each open normal $N$, the images $PN/N$ and $QN/N$ are Sylow $p$-subgroups of the finite group $G/N$, hence conjugate. The conjugating elements form a coset of $N$, giving a decreasing family of nonempty closed sets whose intersection (nonempty by compactness) gives the desired $g$.
mathContext: For each open normal $N \trianglelefteq_o G$, define $C_N = \{g \in G : g(PN/N)g^{-1} = QN/N\}$. Each $C_N$ is a nonempty closed subset of $G$ (nonempty by finite Sylow conjugacy). If $N_1 \leq N_2$, then $C_{N_1} \subseteq C_{N_2}$, so $\{C_N\}$ has the finite intersection property. By compactness, $\bigcap_N C_N \neq \emptyset$.

title: Axiom: Frattini Argument for Profinite Groups
content: The profinite Frattini argument states: if $N \trianglelefteq G$ is a closed normal subgroup and $P$ is a Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup of $N$, then $G = N \cdot N_G(P)$. This generalizes the classical Frattini argument from finite group theory and is a key tool for analyzing the structure of profinite groups via their normal subgroups.
mathContext: The classical Frattini argument: if $N \trianglelefteq G$ and $P \in \mathrm{Syl}_p(N)$, then $G = N \cdot N_G(P)$. The proof: for any $g \in G$, $gPg^{-1}$ is also a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $N$ (since $N$ is normal), so $gPg^{-1} = nPn^{-1}$ for some $n \in N$, giving $n^{-1}g \in N_G(P)$.

title: Axiom: Sylow Pro-p Projects to p-Groups
content: States that the image of a Sylow pro-p subgroup under a continuous surjective homomorphism to a finite group is a $p$-group. This is the bridge between profinite and finite Sylow theory: when passing to a finite quotient $G/N$, the Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup $P$ maps to a Sylow $p$-subgroup $P/(P \cap N)$ of the finite group.
mathContext: If $\varphi: G \twoheadrightarrow H$ is a continuous surjection to a finite group and $P$ is a Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup, then $\varphi(P)$ is a $p$-group. In fact, $\varphi(P)$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $H$ when $\varphi$ is the quotient map $G \to G/N$.

title: Axiom: Distinct Primes Give Trivial Intersection
content: For distinct primes $p \neq q$, the Sylow pro-$p$ and Sylow pro-$q$ subgroups intersect trivially: $P \cap Q = \{e\}$. This follows from the corresponding finite result (a group that is both a $p$-group and a $q$-group must be trivial) lifted through the inverse system.
mathContext: If $P$ is pro-$p$ and $Q$ is pro-$q$ with $p \neq q$, then $P \cap Q$ is both pro-$p$ and pro-$q$. Every finite quotient of $P \cap Q$ has order dividing both a power of $p$ and a power of $q$, hence has order 1. So $P \cap Q$ is trivial.
prerequisites: p-groups and q-groups for distinct primes

title: Compactness of Sylow Pro-p Subgroups
content: A one-line proof that Sylow pro-p subgroups of compact groups are compact: a closed subset of a compact space is compact. This uses Mathlib's `IsClosed.isCompact` lemma directly. The compactness of Sylow pro-p subgroups is crucial because many profinite arguments (such as the conjugacy proof) rely on the finite intersection property for compact sets.
mathContext: In a compact topological space $X$, every closed subset $C \subseteq X$ is compact. Since a Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup $P$ is closed by definition, $P$ is compact in any compact ambient group.

title: Trivial Subgroup is Pro-p
content: Proves that the trivial subgroup $\{e\}$ (denoted $\bot$ in Mathlib's lattice of subgroups) is a closed pro-p subgroup for any prime $p$. Closedness follows from $\{e\}$ being a singleton in a T2 (Hausdorff) space. For the pro-p condition: the trivial group has a unique quotient by any subgroup, so the index is always 1 = $p^0$. The proof constructs this by showing the quotient $\bot / N$ is subsingleton (all elements of $\bot$ are equal), then deriving `Nat.card_unique`.
mathContext: The trivial group $\{e\}$ is pro-$p$ for every prime $p$ because its only finite quotient is the trivial group, which has order $1 = p^0$. This is the base case for Zorn's lemma in the existence proof: the poset of closed pro-$p$ subgroups is nonempty.

title: Uniqueness Implies Normality (sorry)
content: States that if a profinite group has a unique Sylow pro-p subgroup, then that subgroup is normal. The proof is incomplete (sorry): the full argument requires constructing the conjugate $gPg^{-1}$ as a `SylowProP` structure (showing it is closed, pro-p, and maximal), then applying the uniqueness hypothesis to conclude $gPg^{-1} = P$. This is the only remaining sorry in the formalization.
mathContext: If $P$ is the unique Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup of $G$, then for any $g \in G$, $gPg^{-1}$ is also a Sylow pro-$p$ subgroup (conjugation preserves closedness, pro-$p$, and maximality). By uniqueness, $gPg^{-1} = P$, so $P \trianglelefteq G$.

title: IsProP Equivalent to IsPGroup for Finite Groups
content: The central bridge theorem: for a finite group $G$ with discrete topology, being pro-$p$ is equivalent to being a $p$-group. The forward direction extracts the index of $\bot$ (which equals $|G|$) from the pro-$p$ condition and applies `IsPGroup.of_card`. The reverse uses `IsPGroup.to_quotient` to show every quotient of a $p$-group is a $p$-group. In discrete topology, every subset is open, so the only open normal subgroup that matters is $\bot$ itself.
mathContext: For a finite group $G$ with discrete topology, the only open normal subgroups are all subgroups (since every set is open). But $\mathrm{IsProP}$ only needs $[G:\bot] = |G| = p^k$, which is exactly $\mathrm{IsPGroup}$. Conversely, if $G$ is a $p$-group, every quotient $G/N$ has $p$-power order by Lagrange's theorem.

title: Classical Sylow Subgroups are Pro-p
content: Shows that every classical Sylow $p$-subgroup of a finite group (with discrete topology) is both closed and pro-p. Closedness is trivial in discrete topology (every subset is closed). The pro-p condition follows from `IsPGroup.to_quotient`: since a Sylow $p$-subgroup is a $p$-group, all its quotients are $p$-groups, so every open normal subgroup has $p$-power index.
mathContext: For a finite group $G$, a Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ satisfies $|P| = p^{v_p(|G|)}$ where $v_p$ is the $p$-adic valuation. With discrete topology, $P$ is automatically closed and every quotient $P/N$ is a $p$-group, so $P$ is pro-$p$. This shows the profinite Sylow theory strictly generalizes the classical one.

title: Pro-p Subgroups Have p-Power Order
content: For a finite group, any pro-p subgroup has order equal to a power of $p$. The proof extracts the index of $\bot$ in $H$ (which equals $|H|$) from the pro-p condition and applies it with the discrete topology where every subgroup is open. This is the finite-group consequence of the pro-p definition.
mathContext: If $H \leq G$ is pro-$p$ and $G$ is finite, then $|H| = p^k$ for some $k$. Combined with Lagrange's theorem ($|H| \mid |G|$), this gives $p^k \mid |G|$, recovering the classical constraint on Sylow subgroup orders.

title: Sylow Counting Theorem in Finite Quotients
content: Applies Mathlib's `card_sylow_modEq_one` to show that in any finite group (and hence in any finite quotient of a profinite group), the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups satisfies $n_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$. This is a one-line proof wrapping the existing Mathlib result. In the profinite context, this constraint holds in every finite quotient $G/N$, giving a system of compatible congruences.
mathContext: The third Sylow theorem: $n_p = |\mathrm{Syl}_p(G)| \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$ and $n_p \mid [G:P]$ for any $P \in \mathrm{Syl}_p(G)$. For profinite $G$, this holds in each quotient $G/N$: $n_p(G/N) \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$. The numbers $\{n_p(G/N)\}_N$ form a compatible system in the inverse limit.
